newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: DOUBLE TAX AGREEMENT SIGNED WITH GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: DOUBLE TAX AGREEMENT SIGNED WITH GERMANY.

text.p: Lithuania and Germany signed an agreement to avoid double income and capital taxation on Tuesday.

"This mutually beneficial agreement...will help to create a favourable climate for foreign investments and is an integral part of Lithuania's long-term tax policy," Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said during the signing ceremony.
He said that Germany's direct foreign investments to Lithuania's economy were over 330 million litas and accounted for 12 percent of total direct investments as of April 1.

"The trade turnover between Lithuania and Germany was 1.8 billion German marks last year and if we suceed the turnover will rise to around 2.3-2.5 billion German marks," the German ambassador to Lithuania, Ulrich Rozengarten, said.
According to the agreement no tax payer in the two countries will be subject to higher taxes than in his resident country, Rozengarten added.
Shemeta said the agreement will allow information exchange between tax officials in the two countries and he expected it would improve tax administration in general.
The agreement has to be ratified by the parliaments of both countries.
Lithuania has signed double taxation avoidance agreements with 13 countries, Shemeta said.
